title: the washed letter

opening.dialogue: A life is a sending, and the machines at Saduek Sak 24 send everything through water first. Mae Tim folds a camp worker's shirt and a letter falls out of the pocket, soft as a leaf.
She holds the letter up to the fan light. The ink has run to the edges. 'A bus she finally boarded at fifty-eight,' she says, 'and it still cannot read Burmese.'
She pins it to the lost-and-found board beside a single glove and a child's sock, then steps back. 'Three orphans now. The board is getting full of other people's waiting.'

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She lifts the wet letter from the basket and taps it against the lid, scattering droplets onto the lost-and-found board.
turns.dialogue: You come at midnight with a basket and no word first. Why no call? The board already has three things nobody came back for.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She limps to the bench and lowers herself, one hand flat on the share envelope to keep it from sliding.
turns.dialogue: My ankle went on the wet tile by the dryers. I sprained it chasing a sock. The machines do not care whose ankle.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She turns the tea-stall glass in her hands and looks at the letter on the board, not at Lek.
turns.dialogue: The man who owns that shirt, I know his face and not his name. He washes Sundays, first slot. We do not stay in touch. Nobody on this strip stays in touch with the ones who fold fastest.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She points a bent finger at the permit photo pinned beside the letter, its corner curled from steam.
turns.dialogue: This one, with the red seal and the three spellings of one name — what is it called when a paper knows you better than the counter does?

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She sets the tea glass down and slides the share envelope toward Lek across the folding table.
turns.dialogue: A man called for you at the shop, Sanga said. About a letter. I told him the letter was still in the water. He kept his name in a plastic sleeve, Sanga said, and would not take it out.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She presses the wet letter flat under the tea glass and frowns at the running ink.
turns.dialogue: I thought it was fine to leave it on the board. A letter is a letter. But the ink is going, and a name spelled three ways is still a name.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She lifts the laundry basket lid and peers into the drum where the shirt was washed.
turns.dialogue: What is in there, in the pocket still? A receipt, a coin, a girl with no login waiting six hundred miles. The drum keeps what the pocket forgets.

turns.speaker: char_mae_tim
stage_directions: She stands, ankle stiff, and holds the share envelope out to Lek with both hands.
turns.dialogue: I am heading out now to lock the back gate. Take the envelope and the letter both. The circle paid me; the circle can pay for one more sending.

mae_turn_1.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_1.line: She takes the permit photo off the board and presses it into Lek's hand. 'The man who asked about the letter left this. Keep it dry.'

mae_turn_2.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_2.line: She props her ankle on the bench and pulls the share envelope from under the counter, counting its contents twice.

mae_turn_3.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_3.line: She names the Sunday slot and the exact change he always brings. 'First machine, cold water. He does not speak to anyone.'
mae_turn_3.bubble: The letter's owner washes Sundays, first slot

mae_turn_4.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_4.line: She reads the three spellings aloud, slowly, and shakes her head at the third. 'Verified, but not believed. That is what the counter does.'

mae_turn_5.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_5.line: She pushes the envelope across the table. 'The circle's payout. One member asked to be late, so it is short. Use it as you like.'

mae_turn_6.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_6.line: She lifts the tea glass and the letter stays flat, ink fixed where it dried. Half the address is still legible.

mae_turn_7.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_7.line: She pulls the green rider jacket from the drum and hangs it on the rail. 'Bank's. He will want it before midnight.'
mae_turn_7.bubble: The green rider jacket is out of the wash

mae_turn_8.speaker: char_mae_tim
mae_turn_8.line: She limps to the back gate, then turns. 'The board is full of other people's waiting, teacher. Do not add to it.'

finale.dialogue: She locks the gate and stands under the fan with the board behind her. 'A bus she finally boarded at fifty-eight,' she says, 'and it still runs on other people's change.'
The win's lamp is on at the soi mouth. The letter goes into Lek's pocket, dry now, half an address and three spellings of one name.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Two brass keys on a red plastic fob, worn smooth at the bow from nine years of Sanga's thumb; they open the drawer where the stamps live.

obj_score_report.name: the laminated score report
obj_score_report.description: Exam results laminated against the rain, sixty-eight out of a hundred, the failing margin three points wide and visible through the plastic.

obj_word_notebook.name: the word notebook
obj_word_notebook.description: A pocket notebook with a rubber band, pages soft from handling, other people's words written in Lek's hand with the date and who said them.

obj_permit_photo.name: the permit photo
obj_permit_photo.description: A passport-style photo stapled to a work-permit slip, the name typed three ways across three lines, one corner curled from steam.

obj_green_jacket.name: the green rider jacket
obj_green_jacket.description: A delivery rider's jacket, green gone grey at the cuffs, reflective strip peeling, still warm from the dryer.

obj_ring_light.name: the ring light
obj_ring_light.description: A folding ring light on a bent tripod, one LED dead, used by Je Fah for the nine-minute sell-outs from the shophouse back room.

obj_tea_glass.name: the tea-stall glass
obj_tea_glass.description: A small glass, thick-walled, tea stains at the bottom, borrowed from the camp-gate stall and never returned.

obj_laundry_basket.name: the laundry basket
obj_laundry_basket.description: A plastic basket cracked along one side, holding a camp worker's shirt, a rider's jacket, and a single child's sock.

obj_share_envelope.name: the circle envelope
obj_share_envelope.description: A brown envelope with a share-circle payout inside, short by one member's two weeks, the flap folded twice and licked shut.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_mae_tim
outcomeRules.line: She takes the keys and opens the stamp drawer. 'Sanga's stamps. A letter that waited too long still needs postage.'

outcomeRules.speaker: char_mae_tim
outcomeRules.line: She reads the score report through the plastic and sets it down. 'Three points short, and you still read for the whole soi. The board can hold one more name.'
outcomeRules.bubble: Mae has read the score report

outcomeRules.speaker: char_mae_tim
outcomeRules.line: She flips the notebook to a blank page and writes the Sunday man's three spellings in her own hand. 'Now it is written twice. Go before the ink goes again.'

char_mae_tim: She turns the {item} over once and sets it back on the folding table. 'Not tonight, teacher. The board is full enough.'
She taps the {item} against the lost-and-found board. 'The letter first. Everything else is after the letter.'
She holds the {item} up to the fan light and does not look at Lek. 'Three spellings of one name, and you bring me this instead. Open the stamp drawer.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the night with nothing settled. The machines turn; the board waits.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. Mae watches the wet letter the way clerks watch clocks.
Mae's gaze flicks from the {item} to the letter on the board and back — a route mapped, a postage implied.
